sources.title: Damon et al. — Radiocarbon Dating of the Shroud of Turin (1989)
sources.description: The original three-laboratory dating report, with controls, pretreatment methods and the medieval calibrated interval. All Shroud portions came from one corner strip.

sources.title: Casabianca et al. — Radiocarbon Dating: New Evidence from Raw Data (2019)
sources.description: Reanalysis of released laboratory records and statistical heterogeneity; useful alongside the original report rather than as a fresh cloth date.

sources.title: Fanti, Malfi and Crosilla — Mechanical and Opto-chemical Dating (2015)
sources.description: Open synthesis of FTIR, Raman and mechanical estimates. Read with the local calibration and common-bias audit; the loose fibers are not a new authenticated cloth excision.

sources.title: De Caro et al. — X-ray Dating of a Turin Shroud’s Linen Sample (2022)
sources.description: The WAXS first-century-age argument, including its cellulose-aging model and environmental assumptions. This is an aging comparison rather than direct radiocarbon dating.

sources.title: Schwalbe and Rogers — Physics and Chemistry of the Shroud (1982)
sources.description: STURP-era scientific synthesis of image and material observations. A starting point for checking image-formation claims against the reported measurements.

sources.title: Moraes — Image Formation on the Holy Shroud: A Digital 3D Approach (2025)
sources.description: A digital geometry test of body-versus-relief contact imagery. The model tests a proposed mechanism; it does not identify a medieval maker or reproduce every chemical feature.

sources.title: Andrea Nicolotti — Les tribulations d’un linceul
sources.description: Historian’s public university-hosted account of the Shroud’s documentary history; useful for separating secure medieval records from proposed earlier identifications.

sources.title: Vernon Miller Scientific Photographic Archive
sources.description: Scientific photographs for inspecting what image, bloodstain and illumination claims actually refer to. Consult the archive’s image descriptions and reuse terms.

sources.title: Documentação Crítica de Fátima — Selected Documents (2013)
sources.description: Official critical documentary edition. The linked July interview records the advance promise; the September interview is at PDF page 60. The promise should be distinguished from later detailed solar descriptions.

sources.title: Avelino de Almeida — O Século, 15 October 1917
sources.description: Contemporary correspondent’s report, in a DCF transcription with page scans. Distinguishes his observations, crowd reactions and what other observers said.

sources.title: Avelino de Almeida — Ilustração Portuguesa, 29 October 1917
sources.description: Almeida’s illustrated follow-up, explicitly describing dancing and colors as his own experience. It is another record by the same witness, rather than a new independent observer.

sources.title: José Maria de Almeida Garrett — Detailed Witness Account
sources.description: Detailed witness narrative preserved by the critical edition. Compare its date, provenance and feature inventory with the immediate newspaper reports.

sources.title: Philippe Dalleur — Fátima’s Miracle Photo
sources.description: Proponent’s photographic argument, with links to its geometric method and validation examples. Read beside the local camera-assumptions and shadow-correspondence audits.

sources.title: Criminisi, Reid and Zisserman — Single View Metrology (1999)
sources.description: Primary computer-vision method paper on extracting geometry from one image. Supplies methodological context; it is not a study of the Fátima photograph.

sources.title: William Farid Basili — Ministry of Tourism Report, 30 April 1968
sources.description: Archive translation of a contemporary institutional report; Arabic scan pages were retained in the research. Its first-night narrative is not automatically the author’s firsthand observation.

sources.title: Three-priest Investigation Report, 30 April 1968
sources.description: Contemporary investigation report reproduced with original Arabic scans. The modern English translation overstates some clerical titles; the signatories were priests.

sources.title: Coptic Patriarchal Statement, 4 May 1968
sources.description: Formal church statement documenting the institution’s conclusion. It should be distinguished from the separate observations and investigation reports on which it relies.

sources.title: Watani Newspaper, 5 May 1968
sources.description: Contemporary reporting preserved with English translation and Arabic page scans. Useful for named witnesses, medical claims and what was publicly asserted at the time.

sources.title: Cynthia Nelson — The Virgin of Zeitoun (1973)
sources.description: Anthropologist’s published account of visits and social setting. Preserves ambiguity and false alarms as well as testimony; the original journal article was inspected in the research.

sources.title: Gregorios Encyclopedia, Volume 20 — Original Arabic Appendix
sources.description: Arabic compilation, legal deposit 2007, with attributed witness extracts in its appendix. The extracts are not facsimiles of individually signed contemporary witness forms.

sources.title: Gerardo Di Flumeri — Le stigmate di Padre Pio, Documentary Edition (1995)
sources.description: Capuchin-edited collection reproducing physician reports and testimony. Relevant clinical records were read; the original handwritten documents were not inspected.

sources.title: Francesco Galofaro — Medicine and Mysticism in Pio’s Stigmata (2020)
sources.description: University-hosted analysis comparing the medical and cause records. A secondary documentary analysis, rather than another examination of Pio’s wounds.

sources.title: Holy Office Declaration, 31 May 1923
sources.description: Original Acta Apostolicae Sedis declaration at printed page 356. Documents the historical judgment that supernatural character had not been established; it is not a clinical fraud diagnosis.

sources.title: Pietro Gerardo Violi — Consiglia De Martino Clinical Reconstruction
sources.description: Nephrologist and postulation collaborator’s reconstruction of the beatification healing. Read beside the local audit of imaging, timing and cervical-swelling comparators.

sources.title: Pietro Gerardo Violi — Matteo Pio Colella Clinical Reconstruction
sources.description: Postulation-linked clinical narrative of the canonization healing, with treating-team and illness chronology leads. It is not the complete ICU chart.

sources.title: Sanctuary of Lourdes — Recognized Healing Cases
sources.description: Official case hub used to screen 72 published entries in the November 2026 audit. The brief entries are a discovery index, not the underlying medical dossiers.

sources.title: Jim Garner — Lourdes, CMAJ (1974)
sources.description: Journal report including Micheli and Traynor and published radiograph reproductions. Garner was a journalist/editor and describes restricted access to original records.

sources.title: Barbara A. Neilan — Vittorio Micheli Clinical Account (2013)
sources.description: Clinical secondary account derived with permission from Salmon’s medical report. The article contains no actual image plates; use Garner for the recovered radiograph reproductions.

sources.title: Archbishop Malcolm McMahon — John Traynor Declaration (2024)
sources.description: Complete two-page institutional account of the archival review and recognition. For the original 1926 medical minutes, follow the local audit’s source register.

sources.title: Nairobi 1988 — Contemporary Newspaper Reproduction Index
sources.description: Hub for Kenya Times and Sunday Times reproductions about the robed visitor. Contemporary reporting can be checked separately from later supernatural interpretations.

sources.title: T. Jayaraman — Behind the Milk-drinking Miracle
sources.description: Physicist’s account of investigating the 1995 milk event, including replication and runoff evidence. Compare what was experimentally shown with the original public claims.

sources.title: Rungrawee Chalermsripinyorat — Dhammakaya Study (2002)
sources.description: University-hosted study of the movement and controversy. Includes a solar-event witness quotation through The Nation; it is not an independently controlled investigation of the event.

sources.title: Sufi Piercing Case — Original Medical Citation (2001)
sources.description: PubMed record for the cheek-piercing case. The original full article was not recovered; the local follow-up distinguishes its abstract from a later firsthand chapter and unresolved injury baselines.

sources.title: Raguram et al. — Traditional Community Resources for Mental Health (BMJ, 2002)
sources.description: Primary observational study of psychiatric outcomes at a Hindu healing temple. Relevant to comparative healing, with a different endpoint from reversal of destructive bodily lesions.

sources.title: Douay-Rheims Bible — Public-domain Source Text
sources.description: Source edition for the local 105-group passage collection. Its register keeps reference, speaker, verse text and category together, including signs and warnings about deception.

sources.title: John 10 — Believe the Works
sources.description: Read verses 21, 25, 32 and 37–38 in context: Jesus appeals to his works as testimony. One of the central passages in the biblical preamble.

sources.title: Matthew 24 — Signs and Discernment
sources.description: Context for warnings about deceptive signs and claims. Read alongside the passages appealing to miracles rather than treating either group in isolation.

sources.title: Fairfield and Charman — Explicit Bayesian Analysis for Process Tracing (2017)
sources.description: Methodological paper on weighing evidence and rival explanations with explicit assumptions. Provides tools for a cumulative argument without supplying miracle-specific probabilities.

sources.title: Xie and Hayes — Sensitivity to Evidential Dependencies (2022)
sources.description: Experimental work on judgments under evidence dependence. Useful for checking whether multiple reports or methods add independent information.
